For each zero-minimum affine restriction, inverse integrability and bounded concave section root force the endpoint density to vanish. The root is nondecreasing near zero by secant slopes. Its integral against ds/s on [t,sqrt(t)] bounds g(t)|log t|/2, and the same limit at ct controls both old-collar integrals. In dimension one inverse integrability rules out endpoint zeros.

For the new logarithm, in sheared coordinates the interpolation toward (0,b) sends every old collar projection q to a multiplier in [1/2,1] times q in the section at 2ct. That section contains zero. The tilted height has Jacobian derivative 1+O(t) in the transverse direction. The projected area bound O(g(2ct)) times the integral of |log r| on (0,Ct] is o(t), without bounding the tilted log by the old log pointwise.

The same affine index minimizes before and after the common tilt. Outside the collar the pointwise difference quotient converges and is dominated by 2||h||/L. For the floor, the single-height integral of log(1+eta/r) on (0,B] equals B log(1+eta/B)+eta log(1+B/eta), so eta=t^2 costs o(t). The zero old gradient case has a strictly positive constant restriction.

The inner homothety gives O(t) displacement from fixed interior centers and common inballs for old compact interior mark sets. Positive L old boundary points are eventually unchanged, while any positive-area zero face would force divergence of the inverse integral. The cap and moment estimates then follow from bounded integrands and o(t) lost volume.

The new hypothesis K_z=C_z at every old site makes S_t the exact sampled set of the convex cut. The inner homothety keeps each site and lattice-completeness excludes new sites. Every combination of its prescribed sections at a sampled base lies in that exact section, which proves compatibility.

dependencies.hypotheses: At each old or retained mark the corresponding sampled body is compact, convex and full-dimensional and the mark is interior. The accepted unique minimizer has affine denominator at least 1/(d+1) on its own body. Uniform inballs bound the norms of the parameters, and Hausdorff O(t) extends the new minimizer's floor to 1/[2(d+1)] on the old body. Testing the two actual minimizers therefore bounds the change by a constant times the removed volume.

overlap.comparison: The older moving-body result assumes a strictly positive limiting parameter and controls optimized sequences. It gives neither an actual signed affine tilt at a parameter vanishing on a face nor the fixed-pair retained tilted-log derivative.
